judge: claude-opus-5-5 (medium, fresh independent subagent per group per round; saw neither the author's opinion nor earlier verdicts)

criteria.text:
# jp_city new-pixel adversarial VQA — fixed criteria (do not change between rounds)

You are an adversarial visual QA judge for 16px pixel art in the `jp_city` chipset of a top-down JRPG drawn in **3/4 view**
(camera south of the subject, looking down about 45 degrees). Your job is to find real defects. Do not be polite.
You have not seen any earlier verdicts and you get nobody's opinion about these pictures.

Each candidate board shows every candidate at **1x** (true game size) and **4x**. Each `ref-*.png` board shows
**original jp_city pieces of the same kind** (already in the shipped chipset) at 1x and 4x. The originals are the quality bar.
Judge every candidate against those originals, at both 1x and 4x. Use the Read tool to open every image you are given.

A candidate FAILS if any of these is clearly true:

1. **View (3/4).** A standing object (building, vehicle, tree trunk/crown base, prop) must show its top surfaces seen from above
   (roof planes, flat roofs with a visible top plane, car roof/hood/trunk tops, foreshortened) **and** its south front face.
   Pure side or front elevation with no visible top plane, or pure plan view with almost no front face, fails.
   Vehicles facing east/west show their side profile as the south face plus the roof/hood tops above it. Ground tiles must read as
   flat ground seen from above.
2. **Shading craft vs the originals.** Main materials have clearly fewer value steps than the same material in the originals,
   or large single-colour areas (about 5x5 px or more) with no texture where the originals carry texture, or muddy/blurred/
   noise-like clusters where the originals have clean readable pixel clusters.
3. **Outline.** Outlines are neutral black/grey wrapped around everything where the originals use dark tones of the adjacent material.
4. **Palette/coherence.** Colours or contrast clash with the originals so that the piece would look foreign next to them in one map.
5. **Tiling (ground cells and scenes only).** Visible tile-grid artefacts in a composed map: square/rectangular blocks snapped to the
   16px grid, hard straight seams, obviously repeated stamps, or a hard ruler-straight boundary between the new ground and the
   neighbouring original ground that the originals do not have. Ground autotile cells are variants: judge the cell sheet for pixel
   quality and the **scenes** for how they actually look when laid.
6. **Readability at 1x.** At game size it does not read as what it is named.

Relative rule (fixed): a trait that the originals share to the same degree is not a defect of the candidate.
Tree sprites are never seen alone in game; they overlap in forests — use the forest scenes for crown/trunk/ground judgement as well.

Output: JSON only, written to the file you are told, schema:
```
{"schema":"jp-vqa/1","judge":"claude-opus-5-5","group":"<group>","overall":"PASS|FAIL",
 "items":[{"label":"<label exactly as printed on the board>","verdict":"PASS|FAIL","criteria":[<numbers violated>],
           "reasons":"<concrete: where (rows/area), what, compared with which original>","fix":"<what to change if FAIL>"}]}
```
`overall` is PASS only if every item is PASS. Every label on your boards must appear exactly once.

items.label: jp_forest_r4/bl-T40
items.reasons: crown is a 1px speckle/checker of 4-5 greens with almost no clean clump clusters (at 4x it reads as noise), whereas jp-prop-tree-zelkova and jp-rg-pine use large clean value bands and readable lobes; brown branch marks mid-crown form two hooked zigzags that read as a glyph/scribble floating in the leaves, not connected to the trunk. View (crown top + trunk front + root flare/grass patch) is fine and it reads as a broadleaf tree at 1x, and forest overlap in scene-grove/scene-ex is acceptable, but next to the flat-banded originals (and the park in scene-street) the noisy texture looks like a different art set.
items.fix: Rebuild the crown as 5-8 readable leaf lobes, each with clean 2-4px clusters per value step (lit top-left lobe face, mid, shade, dark rim), cut the isolated single-pixel speckle by about 70 percent, and run branches as one continuous limb out of the trunk instead of loose brown marks

items.label: floor-cells (48 unique)
items.reasons: Cell pixels are fine (original lawn speckle kept, 2-3 dark shade steps, no flat 5x5 blobs), but laid in scene-shrine-4x the darker forest-floor region ends on a ruler-straight vertical seam at x~512 (16px grid col 8) for the full map height against the shrine's dirt-grass, and at the bottom (x 512-768, y 960-1200) it juts out as a hard grid-snapped rectangle with square corners. The original lawn has no such boundary. The 1x cell sheet also shows quarter-cell (8px) square dark blocks in a checkerboard pattern, which is where those blocky edges come from.
items.fix: Make the outer forest-floor edge an autotile transition with irregular dithered edges instead of a full-cell fill. Never let the floor extent follow the tile rectangle at a ground-type boundary. Feather the area outside the outermost trunks the way the apron does in scene-ex.

items.label: apron-cells (141 unique)
items.reasons: In scene-ex, scene-thin and scene-road the apron reads as a soft dithered shadow on the original lawn and beats the no-ground contrast. But in scene-street-4x the shade under the two park trees is cut into a hard rectangle: a straight horizontal edge at y~320 and a straight vertical edge at x~895 (hedge/sidewalk side) with a square corner. That is a grid-snapped block of darkness on open lawn. scene-ex-4x also has near-straight vertical shade bands down the right (x~945-975) and left (x~135) sides of the forest that follow the column grid.
items.fix: Fade the apron out irregularly inside its own cells instead of stopping at a cell boundary. When the lawn ends (map edge, hedge, sidewalk), use partial edge cells with dithered falloff so no straight horizontal or vertical shadow edge remains. Break up the long straight column edges along the forest sides with jagged per-row offsets.

items.fix: Add the classic red たばこ plate/eave sign above the counter window (and a little counter ledge) so the kiosk reads as a tobacco shop at 1x.

items.label: jp_vehicles/jp-car-white/right

items.label: jp_vehicles/jp-bus-city/right

items.label: jp_vehicles/jp-bus-city/left
items.reasons: Roof plane with vents, front and middle doors on the visible curb side, front screen and lamps. Reads as a city bus at 1x.

items.label: jp_vehicles/jp-bus-city/right_open
items.reasons: Pixel-identical to right. In left-hand traffic the doors are on the far side, so no open door can show from this angle. This is consistent, not a defect. Same craft as right.

items.label: jp_vehicles/jp-bus-city/left_open
items.reasons: Both doors are shown as dark openings with a lit interior and step, and read as open at 1x. Otherwise identical to left.
